content:
customer_jd: hitting a 413 on /v1/rerank — body says \"Payload Too Large\" but our payload is ~2MB and we've been below limits before. any hints?

maria_support: sorry about that — can you paste a redacted curl and the count of documents you send? also which model/route are you hitting? :thinking_face:

customer_jd: curl looks like:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
 -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
 -d '{"query":"...long user query...","documents":[{"id":"1","text":"..."}, {"id":"2","text":"..."}, ...]}'
```
We send ~180 short docs (~800 chars each) and a 2k char query. model param not provided (using default).

maria_support: thanks — two quick checks: 1) are you using the `passages` field vs `documents`? 2) can you try removing attachments/metadata and re-send just texts to see if it's size vs doc count?

customer_jd: tried minimal body (only id+text) still 413. when I chunk down to 50 docs it works. so seems like doc count triggers it.

kevin_sre: tagging in infra to triage. @raj_backend — do we have a hard per-request doc count cap or combined token budget for rerank?

raj_backend: confirmed — backend enforces two limits for rerank at the gateway layer: (A) max_documents_per_request = 100, (B) combined_tokens_budget = 30_000 tokens. The gateway currently returns a generic 413 for any request larger than its configured client_max_body_size, which is how this surfaces.

kevin_sre: so the 413 is ambiguous — customer thinks it's body size, but it's doc count/tokens causing internal early rejection. we should clarify UX.

maria_support: @customer_jd sorry for the confusion — practical workarounds: 1) chunk docs into batches <=100 and call rerank on each batch (then merge scores), 2) prefilter with embeddings/search to narrow candidate docs to top-K, or 3) truncate long docs / use passage-splitting. would you like a sample snippet to do chunked rerank? :+1:

customer_jd: a sample would be great. ideally less round-trips.

maria_support: here's a quick client-side pattern (pseudo):
```
// split docs into batches of 80
for batch in batches(docs, 80):
  resp = POST /v1/rerank {query, documents: batch}
  collect scores
// stitch results, sort by score
```
If latency is a concern, run the batch calls in parallel and merge.

raj_backend: engineering note for follow-up: gateway currently uses nginx client_max_body_size and a catch-all 413 path. We should surface structured JSON with a code for the limit violated: e.g. `{\"error\":{\"type\":\"limit_exceeded\",\"limit\":\"max_documents\",\"allowed\":100}}` or `{"type":"limit_exceeded","limit":"combined_tokens","allowed":30000}`. This will help support and customers.

emily_product: adding to product backlog: change 413 responses for rerank to explain whether doc count or token budget was hit and include suggested remediation (chunk docs, use embeddings prefilter). Also add client-side helper snippet to docs.

maria_support: @customer_jd quick question — can you share the exact response body you saw? was it plain HTML from nginx or JSON?

customer_jd: it was HTML page starting with \"413 Request Entity Too Large\" and no JSON.

maria_support: okay that matches. will escalate to eng to change gateway behavior. in the meantime I'll document the workarounds in a KB and send a short email with code samples.

raj_backend: timeline: I'll open a PR to handle limit-checks upstream of nginx and return structured 400/413 within 48h. deploy-bot will kick off staging tests.

deploy-bot: deploy started for branch \"rerank/limit-errors-json\" -> staging (job id: 84732) :rocket:

kevin_sre: thanks everyone. @customer_jd let us know if you want us to proactively chunk and merge results on our side (we can do a temporary assist for your account while the API fix ships).

customer_jd: that would be awesome — yes please. thanks team! :pray:
